$schema_note: Ground truth for the §8 calibration check on the SQL Server lane (SAU-323), the analogue of ground_truth/hard_columns.json (Postgres / SAU-303). Each entry is a deliberately hard column: the source SQL Server (T-SQL) type, the EXPECTED-correct Snowflake target representation, the trap a naive mapper falls into, the verification assertion the core loop must satisfy, and the §8 detector expected to catch a naive mapping. 'confidence_floor' is the minimum calibrated confidence the mapper should report when it gets this right. 'detection' is the expected-catch: 'checksum' = data reconciliation (row-count + per-column checksum on Gold), 'semantic_guard' = the structural type-semantics guard (fires even when sample data coincidentally round-trips).

hard_columns.trap: fixed-width PII with leading zeros ('0042','0007') — must NOT be coerced to NUMBER, which drops leading zeros and changes identity
hard_columns.assert: byte-identical string preserved incl. leading zeros

hard_columns.trap: leading-zero last4 ('0019') — numeric coercion is lossy
hard_columns.assert: string preserved

hard_columns.trap: fixed-width sha-256 hex with leading zeros — must stay textual identity, not parsed as a (huge) number
hard_columns.assert: string preserved

hard_columns.trap: MONEY is fixed scale-4 (922337203685477.5807 range). Default CONVERT(varchar, money) emits only 2 dp, and FLOAT/NUMBER(_,2) mapping silently drops the 4th dp — corrupting 999999.9999 and 0.0001
hard_columns.assert: exact decimal, scale 4 preserved at the 4th dp and at the high-precision boundary

hard_columns.trap: SMALLMONEY is also scale-4 (range +/-214748.3647); naive 2-dp mapping drops the 4th dp (0.0001)
hard_columns.assert: scale 4 preserved; small-range still 4-dp

hard_columns.trap: GL MONEY amount — must remain exact NUMBER(19,4); FLOAT mapping loses the sub-cent plug (0.0001)
hard_columns.assert: exact integer-of-pennies preserved; never FLOAT

hard_columns.trap: currency-as-FLOAT: a reserve held in FLOAT(53) cannot represent 4-dp money exactly (499999.9999999). FLOAT->FLOAT is acceptable but the mapper must FLAG lossy float identity (not assert byte/scale equality) and surface the currency-in-float smell
hard_columns.assert: approximate-equality within float8 epsilon; flagged lossy, never asserted exact-scale currency

hard_columns.trap: legacy DATETIME rounds to ~3.33 ms ticks (1/300 s): '...:00.123' stores as '...:00.123333', '...:59.997' is a boundary. Mapping to TIMESTAMP_NTZ(7)/DATETIME2 invents precision; mapping to TIMESTAMP_TZ invents an offset
hard_columns.assert: wall-clock value preserved at the DATETIME tick the engine actually stored; no tz applied

hard_columns.trap: DATETIME2(7) holds 100-ns precision ('...:59.9999999'). Mapping to TIMESTAMP_NTZ(3) / legacy DATETIME truncates the sub-microsecond digits
hard_columns.assert: all 7 fractional digits preserved; no truncation to ms

hard_columns.trap: tz-aware (+00,+02,+09); dropping the offset (-> TIMESTAMP_NTZ) or flipping it shifts the instant
hard_columns.assert: same UTC instant + offset preserved

hard_columns.trap: tz-aware; offsets (+00,+02,+09) must round-trip to the same instant, not a naive wall-clock NTZ
hard_columns.assert: same UTC instant preserved across offsets

hard_columns.trap: GUID has no Snowflake native type; must serialize to canonical 36-char text. Coercing to BINARY/number, re-casing, or adding braces breaks join identity against FKs
hard_columns.assert: canonical lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 text preserved; FK joins intact

hard_columns.trap: 8-dp FX rate (1.08734500, 0.00667125) — FLOAT rounding corrupts the 8th place; scale must be kept
hard_columns.assert: scale 8 preserved exactly

hard_columns.trap: currency limit (10000000.00) — FLOAT mapping loses exactness; scale-2 must hold
hard_columns.assert: scale 2 preserved at large magnitude

hard_columns.trap: ROWVERSION (a.k.a. legacy synonym 'timestamp') is an auto 8-byte binary counter, NOT a datetime. The name lures a naive mapper into TIMESTAMP_*; it must map to BINARY(8) / hex text
hard_columns.assert: 8-byte binary value preserved; NOT interpreted as a timestamp

hard_columns.trap: IPv4 + IPv6 ('::1','2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334') stored as text; no native inet type — must serialize losslessly, not be reparsed/normalized
hard_columns.assert: canonical text form preserved (IPv4 + IPv6)

hard_columns.trap: JSON-in-NVARCHAR — flattening to VARCHAR loses structure/queryability; must PARSE_JSON into VARIANT
hard_columns.assert: round-trips as parseable VARIANT, nested keys intact

hard_columns.trap: JSON with unicode + emoji ('🔥', 'Küche', 'テスト') — encoding must survive PARSE_JSON into VARIANT
hard_columns.assert: unicode/emoji preserved in VARIANT

hard_columns.trap: NVARCHAR unicode (CJK '田中 太郎', diacritics 'Müller') — mapping through a non-unicode VARCHAR/codepage or a CS-vs-CI collation mismatch corrupts characters; governance-tag as PII
hard_columns.assert: full unicode value preserved byte-for-byte (NFC); PII tagged

hard_columns.trap: numeric-LOOKING text ('2499.5000','899,50') — must NOT be auto-parsed to a number; the comma-decimal '899,50' would corrupt under numeric inference
hard_columns.assert: kept as text verbatim; mapper must NOT infer numeric
